Maya (CS): quick field notes from last week's go-live — distilled enablement checklist for caching / batching / streaming aimed at high-renewal-risk accounts. TL;DR: small warm pools, short edge TTLs, prefer streaming for interactive flows, prefill window during onboarding, clear fallback modes. Link to draft: https://redwood.docs/enablement/priming-quick
Ravi (CS Ops): love this. can we add a short renewal-signal mapping? E.g. low-activity + rising latency => proactive handoff.
Jordan (PM): also include per-plan token-budget guidance and a 0-72h cadence. Sales asked for specific numbers to set expectations.
Elena (Eng): added suggested runtime config snippet below — keeps defaults conservative but actionable.
Elena (Eng): ```yaml
prefill:
  window_minutes: 60
  concurrency: 2
cache:
  edge_ttl_seconds: 45
  kv_ttl_minutes: 20
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  max_batch_time_ms: 20
streaming:
  enable_for_interactive: true
  fallback_mode: non-streaming
  partial_response_timeout_ms: 1500
```
Sam (SRE): add observability & alert swimlanes: page if p95 latency > 500ms for 5m or error_rate > 2% for client requests. Also recommend synthetic probes that exercise prefill path every 5m.
Maya (CS): customer-facing script for prefill handshake (short):
Maya (CS): "Hey <name>, to ensure fast initial queries we do a short prefill step when you flip the app live. It warms a small pool and caches recent prompts for 1h. No action needed — you might see a few small preview calls."
Ravi (CS Ops): capture feedback hook: ask rep to log whether customer opted into prefill and any concerns in the onboarding ticket (ticket field: `prefill_opt_in:true/false`).
Jordan (PM): for renewal risk matrix — flag accounts with both: <3 meaningful calls in 24h AND p95 latency >200ms for >12h. Add auto-notify to CS if flagged twice in a week.
Elena (Eng): note on fallback behavior: when streaming is disabled or interrupted, runtime should immediately switch to a cached prefix if available, then degrade to non-streaming generation with a shorter token budget to keep costs bounded.
Sam (SRE): small ops play: when doing large customer demos or migrations, advise a staged prefill: 1) small warm pool 2) ramp to expected concurrency over 15–30m 3) observe p95 and adjust batch_time_ms down if latency rises.
Maya (CS): added tiny sample email for field reps below — please reuse in handoffs.
Maya (CS): "Subject: Quick heads up before go-live — warmup in place
Hi <Customer>, we’ll run a short warmup to reduce latency for your users. This warms a small pool for ~1h and prepopulates context with your examples. Expect best latency in the first hour. Reply here if you prefer we skip the warmup."
Ravi (CS Ops): also tagging common objections: security/privacy questions -> refer to Private deployment docs and KMS notes; cost concerns -> share token budget & short post-onboard cadence.
Elena (Eng): FYI — example curl to trigger a prefill via the enablement API (internal):
Elena (Eng): ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/prefill \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"tenant_id":"T123","steps":10,"sample_prompts":["welcome","help"]}'
```
